issues.t: Engine stalls when fuel pump fuse blows (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving or won't start at all, as if the tank were empty. The fuel pump fuse is often found blown, and it may blow again after you replace it.
issues.why: A wiring harness for the fuel tank temperature sensor may have been routed in the wrong place at the factory. It can rub through, short out and blow the fuel pump fuse. The City Express is covered along with the Nissan NV200 it is built from (NHTSA campaign 25V676).
issues.next: Look up your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The dealer reroutes the harness or replaces the fuel pump assembly for free. Don't keep swapping fuses or fit a bigger one. Parts have been slow to arrive, so call ahead and ask the dealer to order them.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The Passenger Air Bag Off light stays lit even when an adult is sitting in the front seat, so the front passenger airbag would not go off in a crash.
issues.why: The occupant classification system under the passenger seat can mistake an adult for a child or an empty seat. Nissan recalled 2015-2016 City Express vans with many of its own models and replaces the system's control unit (NHTSA campaign 16V244).
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and book the free repair. Until it's fixed, keep adults out of the front passenger seat if the Off light comes on with someone sitting there.

issues.t: Ignition can slip to accessory and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after hitting a bump, and steering and braking suddenly take more effort.
issues.why: On some 2017 vans with a turn key, a heavy key ring or a jolt from the road can knock the ignition switch from Run to Accessory. Nissan recalled the switch on many of its vans and cars, including the City Express (NHTSA campaign 18V551).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall and have the switch inspected and replaced free. Until then, keep only the van key on the ring and nothing heavy hanging from it.

issues.t: Airbag light or Passenger Air Bag Off light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or flashes, or the Passenger Air Bag Off light comes on with someone in the seat. It often shows up years after the recall work was done.
issues.why: The passenger seat occupant sensor and its control module can fault and store a code such as B00A0. GM issued engineering bulletins asking dealers to investigate flashing airbag lights on this van, and Nissan has a matching bulletin for the NV200. Some owners report that replacement parts are discontinued.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on, so don't ignore it. Ask a Chevrolet or Nissan dealer to check for recalls and bulletins on your VIN; a Nissan dealer may be able to source NV200 parts for the same seat sensor.

issues.t: CVT hesitation or shudder with transmission codes
issues.sym: The van hesitates or lacks power when pulling away, may judder or shudder at low speed, and the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: The CVT can set trouble codes such as P0776, P1715 or P17F0 when its pressure control or belt grip isn't right. Nissan's bulletins for the 2015-2018 NV200 (the same van) call for checking the fluid and updating the transmission software, and replacing the valve body if needed.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the shop to check Nissan bulletins NTB18-077 and NTB19-060 for the NV200. A fluid change and reprogramming fix many vans. Don't tow heavy loads until it's fixed.

issues.t: CVT whine or noise from the transmission
issues.sym: A whine, hum or droning from the transmission as the van speeds up, sometimes with less smooth operation.
issues.why: Some CVT sounds are normal and GM issued a bulletin explaining them. On early vans, Nissan also ran a service campaign to replace the torque converter on NV200s built in the same plant, which the City Express shares.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether your VIN is in any open transmission campaign and whether the sound is normal. Get it checked soon if the noise is getting louder or the van slips or shudders.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge doesn't move, reads empty when the tank has fuel, or gives readings that don't match what you put in. The check engine light may also come on.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel level sensor in the tank or its signal to the engine computer causes a wrong reading. Nissan issued a bulletin on NV200 vans with an inaccurate gauge and stored codes.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. Have the codes read and ask the shop to follow Nissan bulletin NTB22-026; the fuel sender is usually the part replaced.

issues.t: Tires wearing out fast
issues.sym: Front tires wear out far sooner than expected, sometimes in about 10,000 miles.
issues.why: These light vans use special load-range tires, and wear rises if the alignment is off or the van often runs heavy. Nissan revised the wheel alignment specs for this van in 2017.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked to the latest specs and rotate the tires regularly. Keep pressures at the door-sticker setting for your load. Buy tires with the correct load rating, not passenger tires.

issues.t: Clicking from front axles when pulling away
issues.sym: A single click or a few clicks from the front wheels when you pull away or accelerate from a stop, especially after the van has sat.
issues.why: The joint where the axle meets the wheel hub can slip slightly and click. GM bulletin 17-NA-235 and Nissan's matching bulletin fix it by cleaning the joint and adding grease.
issues.next: This is not a safety problem by itself. Ask a shop to do the bulletin repair. If the click turns into a steady clicking when turning, have the CV joints and boots checked.

issues.t: Check engine light for EVAP leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the van drives. A code reader shows P0456, P0455 or P0442.
issues.why: A small vapor leak in the fuel evaporation system, often an O-ring at the vent valve near the tank, a loose fuel cap or a bad purge valve. Nissan has bulletins covering this on the NV200.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap clicks tight first. If the light stays on after a few drives, have the EVAP system smoke-tested; the vent valve O-ring fix is simple.

issues.t: Check engine light for air flow sensor (P0101)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with rough running or weak acceleration. A code reader shows P0101.
issues.why: The mass air flow sensor reading doesn't match what the engine computer expects. Nissan's bulletin NTB15-108 for the NV200 gives the steps, which may include reprogramming before a new sensor.
issues.next: Have the code read and the air filter and intake checked for leaks. Ask the shop to follow the Nissan bulletin before buying a new sensor.

issues.t: Engine computer software update for emissions (Nissan campaign)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. You may get a letter, or the dealer may find an open campaign when the van is in for service.
issues.why: Nissan ran voluntary emissions campaigns to reprogram the engine computer on 2013-2017 and 2018 NV200 vans, which share this van's engine and computer. It's not confirmed whether City Express VINs are included.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan or Chevrolet dealer to check your VIN. The update may be covered and takes about an hour. Some states may require it for emissions inspection.

issues.t: Check engine light with ECM code P0603
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often after the battery was low or disconnected. A code reader shows P0603.
issues.why: The engine computer's memory backup circuit flags a fault, often from low battery voltage or a power interruption. Nissan bulletin NTB16-018 covers this code on the NV200.
issues.next: Test the 12-volt battery and charging first. Then have the shop follow the bulletin; it often clears without replacing the computer.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start after a freezing night
issues.sym: After sitting overnight in sub-freezing weather, the engine cranks but won't start, or the security light stays on. Codes like U1000 or U0100 may be stored.
issues.why: Moisture or a communication glitch between the engine computer and other modules after a cold soak. Chevrolet ran Customer Satisfaction Program 15169 for this, and Nissan has a matching NV200 bulletin.
issues.next: If it happens, have a dealer check whether program 15169 was done on your VIN. The fix may be covered if the program applies to your van.

issues.t: Key binds or won't turn in the ignition
issues.sym: The key is hard to turn or won't turn at all, or it sticks in door locks and the ignition.
issues.why: Keys and lock cylinders wear, especially on fleet vans with many drivers. GM bulletin 16-NA-402 replaces the lock cylinders to fix keys binding, and Nissan has a similar bulletin for worn keys on the NV200.
issues.next: Don't force the key or use pliers. Try a spare key; if it works, the original is worn. A dealer can cut a new key or replace the cylinders.

issues.t: Key won't come out or shifter stuck in Park
issues.sym: You can't remove the key after parking, or the shifter won't move out of Park even with your foot on the brake.
issues.why: The key interlock cable or the brake switch that releases the shifter can be out of adjustment. GM bulletin 16NA271 and a Nissan NV200 bulletin cover adjusting them.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work, since a bad brake switch causes this too. Use the shift lock release slot if you need to move the van, then have the cable and switch adjusted.

issues.t: Doors hard to close in freezing weather
issues.sym: Doors are stiff, won't latch, or bounce back open when temperatures drop below freezing.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze inside the latch or weatherstrip. Nissan issued bulletin NTB16-092 for this on the NV200.
issues.next: Make sure the door is actually latched before driving. A shop can apply the bulletin fix; a de-icer spray in the latch helps meanwhile.

issues.t: Engine vibration from driver-side mount
issues.sym: Extra vibration felt in the cabin at idle or when shifting between Drive and Reverse.
issues.why: The driver-side engine mount can transmit too much vibration. Nissan bulletin NTB15-106 replaces the mount on early vans.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. A broken mount makes a clunk when shifting and should be replaced soon.

issues.t: Clunk from front strut tops when steering
issues.sym: A clunk or pop from the front when steering at low speed or going over bumps.
issues.why: The upper strut mounts can bind and pop. Nissan bulletin NTB14088B covers this on the NV200.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked to rule out worn links or ball joints. The bulletin repair targets the strut mounts.

issues.t: A/C water leaks into the center console
issues.sym: Water on the floor near the center console, wet carpet, or an airbag light after running the A/C.
issues.why: A/C condensation can drip onto the airbag control unit under the console. Nissan ran campaigns (PM664, NTB17-029) to add an insulator and inspect the airbag unit on 2013-2017 NV vans.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for the campaign. Dry the carpet to stop mold, and get any airbag light looked at.

issues.t: No start from low 12-volt battery
issues.sym: Slow cranking, a click with no start, or dim lights, especially in cold weather or after sitting.
issues.why: The battery wears out with age and short trips. GM and Nissan both issued battery testing bulletins for vans that sit or work in cold climates.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. Replace a weak battery before winter, and use a maintainer if the van sits for long periods.

issues.t: Rear cargo door stuck locked
issues.sym: One of the rear cargo doors won't unlock or open, even after a latch repair.
issues.why: The rear door lock actuator or latch linkage can fail or freeze in the locked position.
issues.next: Try the key and the inside lever. If it stays stuck, have a shop check the actuator and linkage from inside the door.
